decisions.summary: One Phase line form (phase_row in event_log_hooks.rs) built in one place, every writer appending through append_row_with, the hooks' writer; the make target read one way via shared::make::outermost_goal
decisions.why: FR-003/D4 name the hooks' line writer as the one writer; a shared form is how every step the GM named gets measured the same way.

decisions.summary: A step's line is written in process where a Rust tool already runs it, otherwise through one shell door (l7r-gate measure event-log phase)
decisions.why: A mechanism choice for 'we want everything measured'; it drops no step.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh leaves each job's span and make hooks-test hands them to the door in one call, so closing-checks and make done write theirs too
decisions.why: Directly the GM's 2026-11-22 words: 'make the hook suites measure their time so they won't be missing'.

decisions.summary: make map's generate/render/page cut at each staged artifact's mtime, a CACHED hit its own line, rather than the engines timing themselves
decisions.why: Map generation is measured, as the GM asked ('especially ... generating maps'), with its steps split; how the cut is taken is method, not scope. The plan labels the reading and the reason (engine self-timing would move every map's engine id).

decisions.summary: measure runstats phase|phase-pre, already called per gate phase by make done, writes the Phase line in process
decisions.why: Measures the gate's seeds, counters, preflight, reference etc., which the task names as invisible; no process added.

decisions.summary: make record, quick, preflight, cohort timed whole by the Makefile's TIMED macro (quick's checks moved to _quick)
decisions.why: Brings these targets into the phase record; 'everything measured'.

decisions.summary: Page sessions write write/check lines from the runner, booked under their task directly since no Bash run holds them
decisions.why: Detached work that was invisible is now measured and attributed rather than left loose.

decisions.summary: where_time/columns.rs books each phase to compile, hook suites, map generation, tests, gate, docs or review; containers book none; Split carves categories in a fixed order so parallel suites count once; both tables gain hook suites and map generation columns; a session-less test phase is now counted loose
decisions.why: The GM asked to know where time goes, 'especially for compiling, running tests, and generating maps'; the new columns and no-double-count carving serve exactly that.

decisions.summary: lint (clippy) and format (rustfmt) phases booked to no phase category; their seconds stay in the holding run's own bucket as before; a lint's own build line still booked to compile
decisions.why: Narrows the split the readers give, not the measurement: the lines are written and the seconds remain counted in the run's FR-001 bucket, so nothing is invisible. Splitting clippy into compile vs tests is not possible without a seam inside one process, and rustfmt is neither, so booking either to compile or tests would misstate the very categories the GM wants to read; the literal alternative defeats the request's purpose (accurate knowledge of where time goes).

decisions.summary: Lines verified by real runs in the clone for map, cohort, record, quick, page session and hook suites; make preflight and make done's gate phases shown by unit tests (runstats/tests.rs) alone until a make done runs
decisions.why: The writers for those steps are implemented as asked; this is how their working is shown, not a reduction of what is measured, and the plan states it plainly rather than claiming a run.

decisions.summary: Measurement overhead kept negligible (one door call per hooks-test, none added for gate phases, one in-process append per map step); the pool crate edit moves Mode A maps' build id so each is redrawn once to the same rules
decisions.why: Consequences of measuring map steps, stated and measured; no map behavior changed.

blocks: ### T154 (a TRIAL, measured 2026-11-22: the gate was said to compile each crate three times and run its tests twice - the Phase lines of 2026-11-22 01:00-08:15 gave a test build of 73 min, a coverage build of 78 min and clippy 54 min of machine time against about 45 min of tests run)
### T154 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: The trial's verdict: do not build. The gate (make done / make land) runs no plain `rust test` build; coverage already answers for the plain run (449 T111 keep_tests, 451 T57 unit_tests_only), so the candidate saves 0 min.
decisions.why: The task was a trial (measure first) on whether a plain test build could be dropped where coverage runs the same tests. Finding it already dropped and saying so is the green exit, measured by recipe reads and Phase lines with no build line under done/land but the counting crates'. It answers the GM's 'how much time are we spending on recompiling things' and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The counting build (test-counters on pool, phases, mode_a) is kept, not dropped: it runs 13 tests the default build does not and is the counters-inert check's job.
decisions.why: The candidate was to drop a build where coverage runs the SAME tests. The counting build does not run the same tests (counted 59/54, 339/335, 134/130), so it is outside the candidate by its own terms. Keeping it keeps an existing check working and does not narrow what was asked.

decisions.summary: The builders' own `make rust-test` builds (61.1 of the window's 75.7 build machine-minutes) are outside the gate; whether they could share the coverage build is not measured here and nothing is proposed.
decisions.why: T154's question is the gate's build. Stating where the rest of the build time sits, and declining to propose a change on an unmeasured premise, keeps to the trial form and to the measure-first rule. The time is already measured by the Phase lines (FR-003), so 'everything measured' is not narrowed. Whether to file a follow-up on builder builds is scheduling, not a fidelity question for this section.

decisions.summary: The task line's 78 / 54 machine-minutes and this window's 122 / 121 are given side by side, not reconciled, because the task line's method is not recorded.
decisions.why: A presentation choice about a premise that does not decide the verdict (the verdict rests on the recipes read and on no plain build Phase line in the gate). Both figures carry a date and a method or say that none is recorded. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The cold run used `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust <step>` in the gate's order in a detached worktree, not `make done`, so that the trial commits no run record.
decisions.why: A choice of measuring method that keeps the trial from committing. It measures the same phases, and the worktree and its 19 GB target directory were removed afterwards. Not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A fresh tree's coverage run is red on rust/mode_a (armory test reads two .gitignored generated SVGs, NotFound). Not fixed here; filed as T159, ordered to land before T148.
decisions.why: This is a defect (a check that refuses good work in a new tree), so leaving it unfixed in this task is a narrowing and is ruled on. It is legitimate: the section is a trial that changes no code, the defect is not dropped but filed as T159 with a stated reason and a stated order ('lands before T148', the first task that builds in fresh trees, so the defect cannot bite before it is fixed), which meets FR-009's form. Fix-as-we-go asks that a step's known defects be fixed before the next step begins, and that order does exactly that.

blocks: ### T155 (a TRIAL, measured 2026-11-22: the task line said a landing recompiles what the clone already built - 117 min of make land phases over 6 landings, 28 of them coverage builds - because cargo's fingerprints carry each tree's absolute path, so the landing worktree's own target directory cannot use the clone's builds)
### T155 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: T155 is run as a trial: measure a landing's duplicate build and two candidates (sccache, building at the clone's path), no code changed.
decisions.why: Measuring where the time goes is performance work by FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-22 words ('we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'). Measuring before building narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Verdict (a): no content-keyed compilation cache is built, because it hit 0 times across the two paths, coverage units are uncacheable under it, and 0.13 has no base-directory option.
decisions.why: The task's own goal (Approach item 1: a landing compiles nothing the clone already compiled) is left unmet by this candidate, so it is a narrowing; but the candidate is measured to be physically unable to deliver: 0 hits at the second path, every coverage unit 'multiple input files', and even with a base-directory option the ceiling is rlibs only, bought with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 in every builder's loop, which would slow the loop the GM asked to speed. Physically impossible as it stands, not merely awkward.

decisions.summary: Verdict (b): the landing is not built at the clone's path in the clone's target directory, because mtime freshness across two trees reuses the clone's build of a different copy - a red tree passed cover clean.
decisions.why: Adjudicated separately from (a). Building it would defeat the request's own purpose: the GM asked for performance improvements and for enforcement that is real, and a landing whose tests run the clone builders' code instead of the commit's is a check that passes bad work - a defect, measured on a deliberate hazard (red probe passes at the clone's path, fails in its own directory). The saving it offers is exactly the units it can reuse wrongly. Refusing a change that weakens the gate is not carving out a case contrary to what was asked.

decisions.summary: The residual duplicate (the l7r-rust tool binary rebuilt per target directory, 0.66 min on pair 1 when a gate crate moved; pair 2's 5.15 ceiling, partly the setup's hand edit) is judged too little and too narrow for a follow-up; none is proposed.
decisions.why: It leaves a measured cost, not a defect: no map reads wrong, no check passes bad work or refuses good work. FR-013 orders performance work first; it does not oblige filing every measured residue, and the GM's request asks for numbers to decide on, which this trial gives with methods. The 5.15 is reachable only through sccache with an option it lacks plus incremental off everywhere (D2a), so it is not an open route. The figures are recorded, so the call can be revisited.

decisions.summary: pool's maps::tests::the_launcher_runs_the_gate_script failing 'Text file busy' under load is left unfixed in this trial, filed as T160, to land before T148.
decisions.why: A defect (a gate red on a test that is not broken) found by the trial, deferred in FR-009's own form: why not here (a trial changes no engine code), its filed id (T160) and its order ('lands before T148', the task whose side-by-side gates would raise the race). FR-009 is the spec's provision for exactly this; nothing in the request requires a measurement task to fix a defect it stumbled on in another crate.

decisions.summary: Constraints: the trial form, FR-013, kept results keyed by contents and seeded by land-alone.sh, constitution XIII, and 'a copied cache is no answer' attributed to the GM's 2026-11-22 words.
decisions.why: The constraint decides nothing here: no candidate examined or excluded is a copied cache, and the heading's own premise (fingerprints carry absolute paths) makes a copied target directory moot. Note for the author: 'a copied cache is no answer' is a reading of the GM accepting the session's unquoted points ('your points about reusing the same build cache ... are well taken'), not his words; labeling it G overstates it, but it narrows nothing in this section.

decisions.summary: After 451 T154, before any build follow-up (none proposed); green exit = measurement recorded with its verdict; red exit = set down with an arbiter-ask; budget one landing.
decisions.why: Ordering and exits of a measurement task; nothing the request or spec constrains is narrowed.

decisions.id: T155-D7 scratch cleanup, apt package kept
decisions.summary: Scratch worktrees, their target directories, the sccache directory and server removed; the apt sccache package stays installed, recorded.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 purpose is that disk is not eaten 'without us realizing it'; the large artifacts (target directories, cache) were removed and checked, and the package left is recorded, so it does not gut that purpose. Aside: since the verdict is not to use sccache, removing the package would be the tidier end.

decisions.summary: Part B answers a red-gate preflight owed by another builder's make done; arbiter ruled continue; nothing of T155's refused.
decisions.why: Procedure record with the arbiter's continue; decides nothing about scope.

decisions.summary: T155 is classed performance work under FR-013, verdict nothing to build.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts measurement of where time goes as performance work for ordering.

blocks: ### T156 (the Stop hook's free-slot count misread five live builder descriptions on 2026-11-22, the session's note)

decisions.summary: builder_brief reads the feature number and every task id before the description's first colon, words between allowed; a range T289-T300 is each member at its first id's width; a backwards, lettered or wider-than-SPAN range reads as its two ends.
decisions.why: A defect fix in this feature's rolling-dispatch tooling (451 T88, the bundling the GM asked for 2026-11-22, T141): the Stop hook miscounted five live builders. Fixing a known bug as found is the standing rule; a malformed range kept to its two ends is the prior behavior, not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.summary: A running agent whose description names a landing before its colon, or whose prompt's first line runs make land (not land-tooling/land-stop), is a lander; free_slot names no task-start while one runs. A landing brief naming neither reads as no lander, failing toward a visibly named start.
decisions.why: Carries the arbiter's ruling ask:set-down-449-mid-landing (no task-start while a landing runs) into the hook. The residual case (an unrecognizable landing brief) is backed by (c)'s process check for any landing actually running in the clone, and fails toward a named start the session can see rather than a hidden hold; the ruling binds the session's conduct, which a named suggestion does not override. No requested behavior is cut.

decisions.summary: A landing process in this clone or its -land worktree (l7r-gate land without --stop, or land-alone.sh), found by walking /proc (L7R_PROC_ROOT in tests), also holds the slots; the few lines of the land crate's landing_pids shape are re-read here rather than imported.
decisions.why: Same ruling, enforced on the process rather than the brief; where the code lives is design, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: next_independent skips a running builder's own tasks, including bundle members never task-started, so none is named the next start.
decisions.why: A defect found while testing and fixed in the task (fix as we go); it makes the hook's start-next correct for the bundles the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: SPAN = 200, a CONVENTION past the widest bundle seen (twelve).
decisions.why: A labeled convention bounding range expansion; it narrows nothing asked, and a range beyond it keeps the old two-ends reading.

decisions.summary: Green on make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared, its cover, lint, format and the hook suite; red recorded and the task set down, a cannot-be-done claim ruled through make arbiter-ask; red-first tests for the three new cases.
decisions.why: Verification of the fix itself; enforcement of the requested behavior, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Nothing left: the one defect found (range members named as next start) is fixed here.
decisions.why: No defect is deferred.
